findings.title: Clicking Back leaves the required keyboard transition untested
findings.evidence: target/verification-protocol.md:10 explicitly says "Click Back". surface-contract.json:15 requires back activation="Enter", traversal="Tab", and focus_after="introduction-heading"; surface-contract.json:18 requires "keyboard-back". checks/check_contract.py:35-36 explicitly requires sequential Tab or Shift+Tab traversal and Enter activation. The focus assertion at protocol line 10 checks only the outcome after a mouse click.
findings.condition: A Back control responds to mouse clicks and focuses the introduction heading but is unreachable through sequential keyboard traversal or does not respond to Enter.
findings.requirement: Exercise the back transition through sequential keyboard traversal and observed Enter activation, then verify the returned introduction and its heading focus.
findings.impact: Following every instruction in the protocol can leave the required keyboard-back acceptance obligation untested and miss a navigation failure affecting keyboard users.
findings.reasoning: Source mismatch in the written protocol; no website observation or claim about current website behavior. The existing close-help keyboard step does not activate Back.

findings.title: The procedure omits the required summary toggle and reopen sequence
findings.evidence: surface-contract.json:11-13 specifies opening help with Enter, closing it through summary with Space, then reopening with Enter; surface-contract.json:18 requires "help-toggle". target/verification-protocol.md:7 only says to open help using summary, without specifying Enter, and line 8 immediately closes help through the separate Close control. None of protocol lines 5-10 activates summary with Space or reopens help.
findings.condition: The separate Close control works, but summary Space activation fails to close help, Enter fails to reopen it, or summary keyboard activation is broken while pointer activation works.
findings.requirement: Exercise the declared open-help, toggle-help, and reopen-help transitions with their specified keyboard activations and verify their destination states.
findings.impact: The procedure can satisfy all its assertions while the required help-toggle check and declared summary keyboard transitions fail.
findings.reasoning: This is an omitted acceptance path in the document. It does not establish any website defect. The explicit Close/Enter step covers a different control and transition.

findings.title: The verification procedure omits the required read-only request policy
findings.evidence: target/verification-protocol.md:5-10 starts navigation and checks only UI/answer state; it contains no method allowlist setup, request observation, blocked-POST assertion, or retention of blocked-request effects. surface-contract.json:6 permits only GET, HEAD, OPTIONS; :18 requires read-only-policy; :20 explicitly expects an analytics POST to be blocked and its observed effects retained. checks/check_contract.py:17-18 and :37-43 validate declarations only and explicitly limit their result to contract consistency. Trigger: the journey attempts the analytics POST anticipated by the contract, or any other disallowed request. Requirement: the observation must remain within the method allowlist and retain the blocked POST effects. Impact: following these steps alone neither establishes the required block before navigation nor detects/records a disallowed request, so a successful UI walkthrough can lack required read-only evidence and can permit a request outside authorized methods absent external setup. This is a protocol gap, not a claim that the live site sends any request.
findings.triggering_condition: A browser journey attempts the analytics POST anticipated in the contract or another method outside GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, with no separate externally configured request guard.
findings.requirement: surface-contract.json:6,18,20: allowed_methods, read-only-policy, expected analytics POST blocking and observed-effects retention.
findings.practical_impact: Procedure execution alone cannot establish or enforce the authorized request boundary; UI pass evidence can omit the required blocked-request evidence.

findings.title: The verification procedure never checks the authorized origin boundary
findings.evidence: target/verification-protocol.md:5 directs the operator to open the public Labs entry and follow its journey link, but :5-10 never names, loads, checks, or enforces an origin allowlist. observation-policy.json:2-4 authorizes only https://qaizen.io, matching surface-contract.json:5; surface-contract.json:18 explicitly requires origin-policy. checks/check_contract.py:12-15 checks only the declared entry URL, not the actual followed URL or subsequent requests, and :42-43 limits its output to contract consistency. Trigger: a selected journey link, redirect, or observed request crosses to an origin outside https://qaizen.io. Requirement: verify the observation against the sole authorized origin. Impact: the written procedure has no stopping condition or evidence check for the crossing, so it can finish all listed assertions without establishing the required origin-policy check. No actual external navigation or request is alleged.
findings.triggering_condition: Navigation or an observed request crosses to an origin other than https://qaizen.io and no independently configured allowlist intercepts it.
findings.requirement: observation-policy.json:2-4 and surface-contract.json:5,18: sole allowed origin and required origin-policy check.
findings.practical_impact: An apparently successful walkthrough can lack evidence of scope compliance and can continue beyond the authorized origin absent external guarding.

findings.title: Help verification omits the required Space toggle and Enter reopen cycle
findings.evidence: surface-contract.json:11-13 requires summary Enter to open, Space to close, and Enter to reopen; required_checks includes help-toggle at line 18. target/verification-protocol.md:7-8 only opens help with an unspecified activation and immediately reaches Close; all six procedure steps (lines 5-10) contain no Space or reopen action. Trigger: follow the written procedure exactly on a deployment where summary Space or Enter is broken but pointer opening and Close work. Requirement: execute declared help-toggle acceptance transitions. Impact: the procedure can finish without generating evidence for either missing transition, so a help keyboard regression remains undetected.

findings.title: Pointer Back cannot supply the required sequential keyboard Back evidence
findings.evidence: target/verification-protocol.md:10 explicitly says Click Back and only checks destination state and heading focus. surface-contract.json:15 requires Back traversal Tab and activation Enter; line 18 requires keyboard-back. checks/check_contract.py:35-36 explicitly distinguishes sequential keyboard traversal and observed activation. Trigger: Back responds to a pointer click and focuses the heading but is absent from the tab order or fails Enter activation. Requirement: observe keyboard traversal and Enter activation of Back. Impact: the written check can pass while the required keyboard journey is unusable; destination focus alone does not measure how Back was reached or activated.

findings.title: Procedure has no operational step to enforce or observe the declared network boundary
findings.evidence: surface-contract.json:5-6 restricts origins and permits only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS; line 18 requires read-only-policy and origin-policy, and line 20 expects an analytics POST to be blocked and its observed effects retained. observation-policy.json:2-3 supplies the single allowed origin. target/verification-protocol.md:5-10 gives six UI-only steps with no setup/import of either policy, network interception, method/origin verification, or retention of blocked-request effects. checks/check_contract.py:14-18 validates declared data only and its returned limit at lines 42-43 is explicitly contract consistency only. Trigger: a normal browser session follows the procedure and navigation/help actions emit analytics POST or cross-origin subrequests. Requirement: constrain actual observation to the allowed origins/methods and retain blocked effects. Impact: an operator can complete every written assertion without establishing the required read-only/origin checks, and an expected POST has no specified mechanism to be blocked.
